notes.text: Security update for MozillaFirefox
notes.title: Title of the patch

notes.text:
This update for MozillaFirefox fixes the following issues:

Update to Firefox Extended Support Release 153.6.0 ESR (MFSA 2026-112, MFSA 2026-120, bsc#1286385):

- CVE-2026-100801: Privilege escalation in the DLL Services component.
- CVE-2026-113470: Cryptographic issue in the Security Block-lists, Allow-lists, and other State component
  (bsc#1286261).
- CVE-2026-117860: Same-origin policy bypass in the DOM: Navigation component.
- CVE-2026-117861: Sandbox escape in the DOM: Navigation component.
- CVE-2026-117862: Privilege escalation due to incorrect boundary conditions in the Networking component.
- CVE-2026-117863: Information disclosure due to uninitialized memory in the Audio/Video component.
- CVE-2026-117864: Sandbox escape in the Form Manager component.
- CVE-2026-117865: Use-after-free in the JavaScript: GC component.

notes.text:
A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream.





Users need to update any Brotli libraries or binaries between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1.

notes.text: Mozilla blocked compromised intermediate eMudhra certificates via OneCRL on the 17th of October which was distributed to clients via RemoteSettings the same day. This update contains the updated OneCRL block list, ensuring clients will block the compromised certificates even if RemoteSettings is disabled by policy or otherwise unavailable in the user's network environment. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 158.0.1, Firefox ESR 153.5.1, Firefox ESR 115.43.1, Thunderbird 158.0.1, Thunderbird 153.5.1, and Firefox 158.0.2.
